correctness.rationale: For each prime p the factor f_p(a)=sum_{j=0}^a p^-3j has adjacent-step ratio bounded by 1+p^-3. Nagura prime-gap intervals give three q>p with sum q^-3>p^-3 for p>=29; five small p=11,13,17,19,23 checked as rational inequalities. Thus tail prime factors overlap and their closure is an interval [1,T]. Heads p=2,3,5,7 have transition exponents (2,1,1,1), yielding 3*2*2*2=24 exact rational intervals. Rigorous integral-test zeta(3) bounds with cutoff200 decide 13 gaps and 10 overlaps. Chinese remainder theorem gives density weights products of (p-1)/p^(a+1) and p^-A, giving the 14 table densities summing 1. Independent exact Fraction arithmetic rebuilt all 24 head options, sorted/merged, certified 14 components, 13 gaps, 10 overlaps, exact rational density list [8/35,4/105,2/35,1/105,2/15,1/30,4/35,2/105,1/35,1/210,2/15,1/30,1/15,1/10]. The infinite prime-tail argument is mathematical, not inferred from computation; Nagura is an external theorem, not newly proved.

final_claim: The topological closure of {sigma_-3(n): n>=1} for the ordinary inverse-cubic divisor sum consists of exactly 14 disjoint closed intervals, each with an explicitly given rational natural density. Prime tail p>=11 spans [1,T] with T=zeta(3)prod_{p=2,3,5,7}(1-p^-3); 24 small-prime valuation options merge through 13 gaps and 10 overlaps into 14 components.
